profile.feeling: Possession and existence — one of the busiest verbs.

senses.def: (colloquial, euphemistic: 有了) to be pregnant

examples.tr: There are lots of tomatoes here.

phrases.text: 有朋自远方来，不亦乐乎
phrases.tr: when friends come from afar, is it not a joy?
phrases.meaning: a classic welcome to visiting friends

phrases.tr: for one with a will, the matter is finally achieved
phrases.meaning: where there is a will, there is a way

synonyms.nuance: to possess (qualities, meaning, features): 具有意义
to own, hold (much or important things): 拥有财富

etymology.text: Phono-semantic compound: phonetic 又 (a hand) + semantic 肉 (‘meat’, now written ⺼). Folk etymology reads it as a hand holding meat, hence ‘to have’.

funFacts: The folk etymology ‘a hand holding meat’ makes a good memory aid, even though the real analysis treats 又 as the sound element.
pitfalls: Negate only with 没: 我没有, never *我不有.
Under negation 一个 is normally dropped: 我没有南瓜 (I have no pumpkin).
subtleties: When a place comes first, 有 means ‘there is’: 冰箱里有黄瓜 ‘there are cucumbers in the fridge’.
有 + a noun can make an adjective: 有名 (famous), 有用 (useful), 有意思 (interesting).
